data.name: each::labs Raises $7M Seed to Power Generative Media Platform
data.summary: The San Francisco startup, founded in June 2024 by engineers Eftal Yurtseven and Canberk Sinangil, announced a $7 million seed round on November 18, 2026, co-led by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and Revo Capital. Their platform connects over 600 AI models for images, video, and audio via a single API, handling automated workflows to bridge the 'imagination gap' between creators' visions and AI outputs. With revenue surging fivefold recently to a $20 million annualized run rate, one million daily generations, and 750 paying customers like ad platforms and VFX studios, the funding will fuel proprietary models, San Francisco hires, and expansions like the no-code each::studio workspace.

data.hook: Sales teams often juggle tabs between CRMs, emails, and notes. OpenAI's new ChatGPT for Sales brings it all into one spot, freeing reps for real conversations.
data.name: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT for Sales with Key Partner Integrations
data.summary: On November 17, OpenAI released ChatGPT for Sales, a plugin with over 30 integrations like Salesforce, HubSpot, and Gong to research accounts, prep meetings, draft outreach, and update CRMs seamlessly. Greg Brockman highlighted how it ties sales tools together, letting users rank targets, spot risks, and suggest next steps while staying in control. The same day, Spara debuted Scout, a Slack-based AI that monitors signals overnight and drafts personalized follow-ups, boosting reply rates from 3.5% to 10.5% in early tests. These tools aim to cut busywork so sellers focus on closing deals.

data.hook: Perplexity AI just committed over 10,000 GPUs to build AI that conducts research on its own—from spotting knowledge gaps to running experiments.
data.name: Perplexity AI Launches Frontier Research with 10,000 GPUs for Autonomous Science
data.summary: On November 16, the company unveiled Perplexity Frontier Research, focusing on multi-agent systems, reinforcement learning, and continual learning to automate the full research process. Results will include openly released papers, models, data, and benchmarks tested in their products, with CEO Aravind Srinivas highlighting plans to integrate findings into user tools. Perplexity also shared crossing $1 billion in annual recurring revenue and launched an Orchestrator API that picks the best model from 45 options for any task. The team is hiring in multiple cities to push toward fully independent AI discovery.

data.hook: Genesis AI's CEO Zhou Xian envisions robots that match human hands in factories and labs, working reliably for years without a hitch.
data.name: Genesis AI Raises $500M for Dexterous Factory Robots
data.summary: The robotics startup secured $500 million in Series A funding at a $3.5 billion valuation, co-led by Premji Invest, Khosla Ventures, and Eclipse, with Nvidia and AMD also joining. Their full-stack system uses sensor gloves to train the GENE model in real tasks, tested in the Genesis World simulator before deploying on the compact Eno robot with foldable panels for precise industrial work. Co-founder Théophile Gervet stressed optimizing data, AI, simulation, and hardware together for reliable performance, setting up pilots now and wider rollout in 2027.

data.hook: Demis Hassabis shared big news from his AI drug company: a massive $5 billion funding round to tackle all diseases faster. It's a bold step toward reimagining how we design medicines.
data.name: Isomorphic Labs Raises $5 Billion to Speed AI Drug Discovery
data.summary: Isomorphic Labs, founded by DeepMind's Demis Hassabis and spun out of Google in 2021, closed an oversubscribed Series C round co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with new backing from Andreessen Horowitz and support from Alphabet and others. The funds will scale their AI engine, IsoDDE, which predicts protein interactions, expand over 20 programs with partners like Eli Lilly and Novartis, and push preclinical successes in oncology and immunology toward clinical trials. This follows a $2.1 billion raise earlier in 2026, signaling strong investor faith in AI's power to slash the years and billions needed for new drugs, even as the field awaits its first approved therapies.

data.hook: A husband-and-wife team in Canberra just unveiled Agentaus 1, a massive 220-billion-parameter AI that keeps all data safely onshore and answers only to its users.
data.name: Australia Launches Sovereign AI Model Agentaus 1
data.summary: Trellis Data released Agentaus 1, scoring 84.4% on the MMLU-Pro benchmark and ranking 43rd worldwide, with strict privacy features like no data training and permanent chat deletion. Built on Australian servers with under $10 million in funding, it offers efficient performance on fewer GPUs and affordable API access starting at $1.15 per million tokens. The launch highlights Australia's focus on data sovereignty, drawing praise for blending capability with local control amid rising privacy concerns.

data.hook: Imagine telling an AI your dream beach getaway, and it handles every detail from booking to price checks. That's the promise of Atlas, the new personal travel agent from ex-Uber and Google leaders.
data.name: Voyage Labs Raises $12M for AI Travel Agent Atlas
data.summary: Manik Gupta, former Uber chief product officer and Google Maps leader, and co-founder Yogesh Jain raised $12 million in seed funding for Voyage Labs and its Atlas AI agent. Led by Kleiner Perkins with SignalFire and others joining, the funds will expand partnerships for flights, hotels, dining, and experiences while growing the team. Atlas takes user ideas—like a ski trip or dinner reservation—researches options, books directly, learns preferences over time, and monitors changes, moving beyond simple suggestions to full trip management. Early beta users are planning trips, with a waitlist open amid excitement over specialized AI for travel.

data.hook: Ivan Burazin of Daytona declared the market for new AI sandbox providers effectively shut for strong venture returns, likening them to rivals of Replit or Lovable.
data.name: AI Sandbox Founder Warns Market Closed for New Ventures
data.summary: Daytona, which scaled from $1 million to $100 million annualized run rate in four quarters with fast-starting sandboxes under 90 milliseconds, sparked debate in the crowded AI infrastructure space. Rivals like Modal hit $300 million run rate on sandboxes within a $1 billion business, while Replit rebuilt its engine for agent isolation. Critics countered that agent swarms and niches like hardware stacks or regional needs keep room for winners, though some see it as posturing amid surging demand.

data.hook: Imagine skipping the airport hassle for a comfy 4-hour robotaxi ride from Boston that lets you work or relax along the way. A post comparing it to a 5.5-hour flight has people rethinking regional trips.
data.name: Cybercab Robotaxi Challenges Short Flights in Travel Debate
data.summary: The post breaks down a Boston journey: airport drives, TSA lines, and baggage claim stretch flying to 5-5.5 hours, while Tesla's door-to-door Cybercab cuts it to about 4 hours. Tesla now invites select buyers for the $29,990 two-seater without steering wheel or pedals, plus a $299 monthly subscription, starting deliveries in Austin this December in limited Texas and Florida zones. Reactions mix excitement for ride-hailing potential with reminders of trains beating drive times, battery range questions, and calls for both Cybercab and Cybertruck ownership.

data.hook: Max Rumpf unveiled SID-2 amid a custom film set with server racks and 100 origami cranes folded from printed documents, showcasing AI's creative boost.
data.name: SID.ai Launches SID-2: Faster, Cheaper AI Search Swarms
data.summary: SID.ai released SID-2 on November 17, a search model using coordinated swarms of AI agents that outperform Anthropic’s Opus and Google’s Astra while running 8x faster and at 20x lower cost. It tackles the data explosion from AI generating an internet’s worth of text daily by 2030 and enterprises hitting petabyte scales. The launch video, built in 12 hours with AI tools, drew positive reactions in the AI community, with the technical report praised as one of the year's strongest. SID-2 is now available via API for testing on tough queries.

data.hook: Imagine AI agents diving straight into a bank's core ledger, fetching data and tweaking settings—all while following strict rules and logging every move.
data.name: Stitch Launches AI Agents Inside Banking Systems
data.summary: Stitch has rolled out Stitch AI, embedding autonomous agents directly into its banking operating system. These agents handle tasks like onboarding, credit checks, and collections using live data, with features like a copilot for plain-language requests, custom agent building, and strict controls such as human approvals for big changes and data masking. The launch tackles legacy system hurdles, letting banks move beyond basic chatbots to real workflow automation in regulated settings. Online reactions blend excitement with memes, like one showing stunned bank staff as AI finally acts on months of meeting talks.

data.hook: Hyperbolic Labs just locked in a $5 million hedge against falling NVIDIA B200 GPU rental prices. It's the first over-the-counter option of its kind in the AI compute world.
data.name: First OTC Put Option Executed on GPU Rental Prices
data.summary: Architect Financial Technologies, Luxor Technology, and Hyperbolic Labs completed the milestone trade, which settles monthly in cash against Silicon Data’s B200 Rental Price Index over a year. Hyperbolic used it to protect future rental revenue amid price swings that hurt operators when rates drop and buyers when they rise. On the same day, Compute Desk raised $45 million in seed funding led by Lightspeed Venture Partners to build clearing infrastructure, price indexes, and settlement tools for a more liquid compute market. Leaders like Hyperbolic's Jasper Zhang hailed it as a vital step for managing volatility in AI's booming demand.

data.hook: Imagine an AI that truly gets your priorities, style, and relationships—without any company owning it. First Person Labs just launched Second to make that real.
data.name: Second Lets You Own Your Personal AI Model
data.summary: First Person Labs unveiled Second on November 17, a portable AI model that runs on your Mac and builds a deep understanding of you from daily activity. AI agents like Claude or iMessage can access it via API for instant context, while you retain full control and ownership. Backed by a $10 million seed round from a16z and Mozilla Ventures, the startup emphasizes privacy through on-device processing and inspectable data, addressing gaps in current assistants. Early users praise how it cuts down on repetitive explanations across tools.

data.hook: AI researchers like OpenAI's Mark Chen ponder how close we are to machines that improve themselves, turning sci-fi into real lab work.
data.name: a16z Podcast Explores AI's Path to Self-Improvement
data.summary: a16z's new 'Working Theory' podcast series kicks off with interviews featuring OpenAI's Mark Chen and Thinking Machines Lab's John Schulman, who explain recursive self-improvement—where AI drives its own research. Chen estimates OpenAI is 80% toward AGI but only 25-50% to full RSI, with 'research taste' from human experience as a major hurdle. A recent Google paper advances this by adding memory to optimizers, boosting scores in coding tasks from 68 to 85. Experts emphasize human-AI teamwork remains key for now.
